title: Weights Embassy: ingest-to-version-anchoring and profile-publish pipeline
creator: Maya Patel
description: Implement an end-to-end pipeline (Weights Embassy) that takes a new open-source model weights bundle through secure intake, deterministic conversion, artifact provenance checks, runtime compatibility validation, and automated publication of a canonical version anchor and performance profile. The goal is predictable onboarding turnaround for community models while minimizing manual triage and preventing regressions in serving behavior.
acceptance_criteria: Secure intake service accepts signed manifests and stores raw artifacts in immutable object store with provenance metadata
Deterministic conversion runs (format normalization + quantization matrix) produce runtime-ready artifacts and a reproducible conversion log
Compatibility smoke tests execute on representative runtime configurations and emit structured telemetry (latency, memory, token throughput, sample outputs)
Automated version anchoring creates a canonical model version (anchor id) with links to artifacts and conversion recipe; anchor is immutable and discoverable in model catalog
Performance profile (latency/throughput/cost per-token) is published to the catalog and triggers a baseline comparison job that flags regressions vs. comparable models
Rollback path: failed anchors or profiles are automatically quarantined and route requests to fallback compatible variant
End-to-end run documented in Playbook with runbook steps, failure modes, and responsible oncall rotation
updates: 2025-01-16: Kickoff meeting with PM and Runtime teams. Agreed on 'anchoring' terminology to avoid confusion with existing internal 'pin' vocabulary.
2025-01-17: Prototype intake API implemented (POST /embassy/ingest) and basic signed-manifest parsing. Stored manifest schema in Confluence: https://confluence.internal/redwood/weights-embassy-schema
2025-01-18: Conversion container image created (gnu+cuda toolchain). Ran deterministic conversion locally for Llama-2-7b and captured conversion digest. Next: make conversion hermetic in CI.
2025-01-18: Decision: use SHA256 of normalized artifact set + conversion recipe as the canonical anchor id. Trade-off: longer IDs but full traceability.
2025-01-19: Integration with telemetry: added structured events for conversion_start, conversion_done, smoke_test_result to existing onboarding pipeline topic in Kafka (topic: onboarding.events).
2025-01-20: QA/Design review requested. Design comment: surface an early warning field in profile UI when latency tail exceeds 99th percentile threshold. Filed follow-up DES-213 in Design backlog.

2025-01-20: Security scan on intake code flagged potential path traversal when unpacking archives; fixed by enforcing safe extraction and adding unit tests. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/weights-embassy/pull/42

2025-01-21: Benchmark harness committed. Initial smoke run results for test-candidate 'redfox-3b' show token throughput within expected band; memory exceeded target on older GPU flavor — opened ENG-120009 to track kernel selection optimization.
2025-01-21: Ops note: added a hard quota for community ingest to avoid noisy neighbors during early rollout (limit: 3 concurrent conversions per org).

2025-01-22: Validation: profile publish flow writes to model-catalog service and triggers baseline-compare job. Baseline job returns 'no-regression' for first two cases. Next: add canary route to monitor real traffic for 48h before enabling dedicated routing.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Malicious or malformed community weights could cause conversion hangs or resource exhaustion. Mitigation: run conversions inside resource-capped sandbox and apply static manifest validation prior to scheduling.

Risk: Automated anchors could lock in a model with latent regressions. Mitigation: require two independent smoke profiles and a manual sign-off flag for high-risk models OR enable a 48h canary monitoring window before turning on production routing.
Risk: Profile instability across hardware variants. Mitigation: publish per-variant profiles and include 'recommended flavors' metadata so routing can pick compatible variants.
next_steps: Stabilize conversion hermetic CI and add deterministic seed tests (owner: Ethan)
Wire canary routing and dashboard alerts for 99th percentile latency regression (owner: Infra)
Finalize public-facing model-catalog schema and docs for external teams (owner: PM)
Plan a 2-week limited beta with Community Program and track ingestion metrics
